channel.title: Morning Score
channel.description: Delivered every Monday by 10 a.m., Weekly Score is your guide to the year-round campaign cycle.

item.title: Why Dems’ late House reaches don’t usually pan out
item.description: House Democrats are pushing into redder territory, but history shows those last-minute moves don’t usually pan out.
item.dc:creator: By Aaron Pellish and Andrew Howard
item.dc:contributor: By Aaron Pellish and Andrew Howard

item.title: Why one GOP pollster thinks a blue wave may wash out
item.description: Democrats are salivating over, and Republicans are bracing for, a potentially massive blue wave. One GOP pollster is urging everyone to calm down.
item.dc:creator: By Aaron Pellish

item.title: Dems are tripling GOP in Spanish-language ad spending
item.description: Democrats are vastly outspending Republicans on Spanish-language ads.
item.dc:creator: By Andrew Howard, Lisa Kashinsky and Samuel Benson
item.dc:contributor: By Andrew Howard, Lisa Kashinsky and Samuel Benson

item.title: The third-party candidates who could play spoiler next month
item.description: There’s a trio of Libertarian candidates who could pull more from Republican candidates in Texas, Iowa and Kansas
item.dc:creator: By Erin Doherty

item.title: The data behind Dems’ new Jeffrey Epstein ads
item.description: Democrats’ top Senate super PAC is flooding the airwaves with ads hitting Republicans on Jeffrey Epstein.
item.dc:creator: By Andrew Howard

item.title: Republicans return to crime messaging
item.description: Republicans are running more ads casting Democrats as soft on crime.
item.dc:creator: By Lisa Kashinsky

item.title: AI isn’t taking over campaign ads… yet
item.description: The airwaves haven’t been flooded with AI-produced campaign ads this cycle. But it may be only a matter of time.
item.dc:creator: By Aaron Pellish

item.title: The 2028 redistricting fight is already kicking off
item.description: The 2026 House maps are finally set, and the fight to redraw in 2028 is already underway.
item.dc:creator: By Aaron Pellish

item.title: What's in a name?
item.description: Sen. Jeanne Shaheen still looms over her daughter Stefany Shaheen's primary campaign in New Hampshire.
item.dc:creator: By Lisa Kashinsky, Jessica Piper and Aaron Pellish
item.dc:contributor: By Lisa Kashinsky, Jessica Piper and Aaron Pellish

item.title: Markey isn’t the only incumbent sweating in Massachusetts
item.description: Democrats’ crusade for change is coming to a head in Massachusetts, where a trio of incumbents are staring down some of the toughest primaries of their careers.
item.dc:creator: By Lisa Kashinsky and Aaron Pellish
item.dc:contributor: By Lisa Kashinsky and Aaron Pellish
